fact: January 1888, temperatures on the Dakota prairie were around sixty degrees before the storm hit
A cold front dropped temperatures forty degrees in minutes
Schoolteachers roped children together and attempted to walk toward town in zero visibility
source: The Children's Blizzard, David Laskin (2004) — multiple accounts of teachers leading roped-together students

fact: Two hundred thirty-five people died, mostly children
source: The Children's Blizzard, David Laskin (2004); National Weather Service estimates range from 235 to over 500

fact: Many victims were found within a short distance of shelter they could not see
source: The Children's Blizzard, David Laskin (2004) — widely documented in contemporary newspaper accounts
